name: Centro de Retiros Karma Kagyu de Tabio
aka: Estupa de la Iluminación en Tabio
tradition: Karma Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Vajrayana Buddhism
technique: Shamatha (calm-abiding) meditation, Mahayana practices (tonglen, refuge, bodhicitta), and Vajrayana preliminary practices (ngöndro, deity meditation) taught progressively
teacherAccess: Monthly retreats are led in person by lay teacher Carlos Velásquez (30+ years teaching Buddhism and meditation in Colombia); visiting Tibetan lamas such as Lama Jampa and Khenpo Tsering Samdup give teachings roughly twice a year.
retreatOptions: Monthly weekend meditation retreats open to all levels (no prior experience required); twice-yearly multi-day retreats with visiting Tibetan teachers.
about: The Karma Kagyu retreat center in Tabio, Cundinamarca, about 45 km from Bogotá, is the dedicated retreat land of Budismo Colombia, a Tibetan Buddhist community founded by lay teacher Carlos Velásquez, who has taught Buddhism and meditation in Colombia for more than 30 years, including as a professor of Tibetan Buddhism at the National University of Colombia. The property is home to the Estupa de la Iluminación de Tabio, a traditional stupa that took five months to build (and 20 years to conceive), housing relics of the Buddha Kashyapa and Shakyamuni alongside thousands of hand-made Buddha statuettes and mantras. Every month the center hosts a weekend meditation retreat open to all levels, progressing from Shamatha (calm-abiding) meditation through Mahayana practices such as tonglen to Vajrayana preliminary practices (ngöndro); roughly twice a year, visiting Tibetan teachers such as Lama Jampa and Khenpo Tsering Samdup lead additional retreats. No prior experience is required, and advance registration with a donation covers lodging, meals, and teachings for the retreat.
schedule: Monthly weekend retreats on the center's land in Tabio combine teaching sessions with guided meditation; twice-yearly multi-day retreats are scheduled around visiting Tibetan teachers.
cost: Donation-based; advance registration and a suggested contribution cover lodging, meals, and teachings for the retreat.
